authority_boundary: This registry indexes reusable assets installed in this repository. Each asset directory remains the source package for its own files; downstream deployment remains a separate reviewed action.

assets.name: AI Engineering Preflight Asset
use_when: Planning AI-assisted software implementation or refactoring.
Creating or updating Python, Rust, or mixed-language repo agent instructions.
Preparing a dry-run rollout of AI preflight files to another repo.
Reviewing long Python scripts or Rust modules for modular encapsulation boundaries.
does_not_apply_when: The task is pure catalog validation with no software engineering or repo-template work.
A downstream repo has not been approved for mutation.
safety_notes: Deployment scripts default to dry-run.
Managed blocks are used for existing agent instruction files.
Collision-prone generated files are written as .candidate files unless force is requested.
Installing the asset in DAD does not authorize deployment to any other repository.

assets.name: lowelltwong-alt Repo Map And Wave Plan
use_when: Planning DAD managed-pointer, mailbox, or preflight-profile rollout across the lowelltwong-alt workspace.
Reviewing candidate wave order before mutating downstream repositories.
Checking which repos require local inventory before any managed pointer or mailbox install.
does_not_apply_when: A downstream repo has not had local authority files refreshed.
The task needs canonical source truth rather than a preliminary GitHub-observed map.
A human has not approved the next wave beyond DAD wave 0.
safety_notes: This packet is a planning seed, not source authority.
Draft PowerShell commands must not be run wholesale.
Wave 0 applies to DAD only and does not run downstream agent install against DAD.
Before waves 1 and later, DAD must refresh local repo paths, authority files, branch state, visibility, and mail policy.
Hooks remain disabled unless separately approved.

assets.name: Python AI Advantage Preflight Asset
use_when: Planning Python AI-assisted implementation, refactoring, or package/API design.
Teaching an AI agent when to use high-leverage Python features with applicability limits.
Creating a Python-specific preflight profile or downstream managed instruction block.
does_not_apply_when: The task is not Python or Python-adjacent.
The target repo has not approved DAD-managed pointers or instruction changes.
The tactic cannot be verified with local tests, type checks, linters, or review.
safety_notes: Installed from the inspected zip without __pycache__ or .pyc files.
Underused-pattern labels are heuristic unless backed by measurement evidence.
Use as candidate DAD guidance; target repos retain local authority and validation requirements.
Do not copy the full asset into downstream repos without explicit approval.

assets.name: DAD Agent Skill Library
use_when: A repo wants to check out a DAD-managed agent skill by pointer or wrapper.
DAD needs to send skill update, retirement, or replacement notices through mail.
A future repo template should know how to discover and refresh agent skills.
does_not_apply_when: The target repo has not approved DAD skill pointers or wrappers.
The task would copy full skill bodies, install plugins, or mutate downstream source files without human approval.
safety_notes: Checkouts default to pointer mode.
Skill mail is candidate evidence and does not install or update target repos.
Private/internal/restricted/unknown-origin skill notices headed to public-facing repos inherit DAD human release gates.
Do not copy full DAD skills into downstream repos without explicit approval.

assets.name: DAD Repo Enrollment And Control Plane
use_when: A persistent repo should receive DAD full governance enrollment in a reviewed wave.
DAD needs to update enrolled repo pointers, maps, hooks, or managed AI guidance.
A future repo template needs daily mail and weekly asset/skill/template/control-plane cadence.
does_not_apply_when: The repo is not present in reviewed enrollment.repos policy.
The task only needs candidate mail delivery under .digital-asset/mail/**.
A human approval ID has not been recorded for full governance install or update.
safety_notes: Enrollment apply/update requires reviewed policy and a human approval ID.
Normal recurring DAD operation remains mailbox-only.
Public-facing repo output omits local absolute paths by default.
Repo renames keep stable repo IDs only when the same contract still applies; repo splits require new enrollment records.

assets.name: Python Underused Idioms AI Coding Card
use_when: An AI agent is writing, refactoring, reviewing, debugging, or researching Python code.
A review wants citable Python idiom IDs with avoid-when limits.
DAD is refreshing Python language guidance from frontier sources.
does_not_apply_when: The target repo's Python version is below the idiom's min_python.
The edit would rewrite working code solely to use an idiom without a task-level reason.
Local repo style authority conflicts with a suggested idiom.
safety_notes: Under-representation claims are heuristic unless measured.
Each idiom carries avoid_when and min_python gates.
Frontier refreshes use pointer-only research intake before changing guidance.

assets.name: Rust Buildout And Python-To-Rust Migration Guide
use_when: A task mentions Rust, performance, parsing speed, a Python hot path, or a possible rewrite.
A repo needs a staged Python-to-Rust migration path with profile and parity gates.
DAD is refreshing Rust language guidance from frontier sources.
does_not_apply_when: No profile evidence identifies a real hot path.
The work is I/O-bound glue or fast-changing prototype logic.
A full port is being considered without human-reviewed load-bearing decision evidence.
safety_notes: Rust recommendations require profiling first.
Replacement claims require same-scope shadow parity before timing claims.
Frontier refreshes use pointer-only research intake before changing guidance.

assets.name: DAD Rust Scan Core And Rollout Pack
use_when: DAD needs deterministic local source inventory, hashing, JSONL observations, or quarantine summaries.
A repo needs DAD's Rust rollout policy, local instruction packet, or target ownership rules.
An agent is validating the first DAD Rust leaf tool before downstream recommendations.
does_not_apply_when: The task needs governance meaning, legal judgment, theological judgment, or model orchestration.
A downstream repo lacks a reviewed local path or is Logos instruction-mail-only.
The Rust output would be treated as source truth rather than candidate observation.
safety_notes: Python remains the orchestrator.
Rust emits candidate observations only.
Downstream apply refuses Logos repos and missing local paths.
DAD lessons must be checked before advising target repos.

assets.name: Exception Capture Completeness Harness
use_when: DAD changes what repos should emit as mail, exceptions, fix outcomes, or usage records.
A repo should prove it would send the right metadata packet without Lowell rescuing it from chat.
Observed outboxes need read-only audit against DAD capture patterns.
does_not_apply_when: The evidence would require copying raw private data, secrets, long logs, or source blobs.
The target repo has not approved DAD pointers or capture-surface checks.
safety_notes: Scenario matches prove expected packet behavior, not source truth.
Observed capture audit is read-only and path-hash-first.
Every reviewed capture rule needs at least one declared synthetic scenario.
v0.2 adds ordinary engineering/data-plane exception capture and unsafe-field regression checks.

assets.name: Exception Learning Readiness Harness
use_when: DAD changes exception learning queue statuses, blockers, fix-outcome validation, or release gates.
A future agent needs proof that weak, mixed, or backfill-only evidence does not become promotion-ready.
The exception lake needs synthetic guardrails before learning from fix outcomes.
does_not_apply_when: The question is whether a repo would emit a packet at all; use the exception capture completeness harness.
The evidence would require copying raw private data, secrets, long logs, or source blobs.
safety_notes: Synthetic readiness checks protect against known false-green queue states.
Passing scenarios do not prove real repo completeness or authorize lesson promotion.
Non-public-origin evidence remains human-release gated for public-facing reuse.

assets.name: Language Frontier Source Radar
use_when: DAD needs to refresh Rust, Python, or mixed-language coding guidance.
A repo finds a new source, technique, crate, package, or idiom worth sending to DAD.
A future language should get a reviewed frontier watch list before becoming DAD guidance.
does_not_apply_when: The source is unknown and no justification is available.
The content would be copied instead of stored as a pointer-only intake candidate.
A recommendation lacks screening, local validation, and applicability limits.
safety_notes: Source cadence is not promotion authority.
All external content still requires screening and human approval before promotion.
Language-frontier mail uses safe summaries, URLs, hashes, and validation ideas only.

assets.name: Language Coding Advantage Registry
use_when: A coding agent needs Python, Rust, or future-language guidance before implementation.
DAD is refreshing frontier language sources or evaluating an overlooked language pattern.
A repo wants to send a language technique, crate, package, or validation idea back to DAD.
does_not_apply_when: The target repo's local style or toolchain authority conflicts with the guidance.
The language idea has no trusted source pointer, validation gate, or applicability limit.
The packet would copy third-party docs, private rows, credentials, logs, or long source blobs.
safety_notes: Language guidance is candidate evidence until reviewed locally.
Underuse and frontier labels are heuristic unless backed by measurement or repeated DAD outcomes.
Adoption requires local validation and repo authority; source trust tiers never authorize copying content.

assets.name: Language Coding Playbooks
use_when: An agent needs a compact Python, Rust, or future-language operational checklist before coding.
DAD is routing frontier language research into a playbook, tactic, asset, or harness eval.
A repo wants to report an overlooked language operation or coding advantage back to DAD.
does_not_apply_when: The target repo's local style or toolchain authority conflicts with the playbook.
The language idea has no proof surface, avoid-when limit, or local validation idea.
The packet would copy third-party docs, private rows, credentials, logs, or long source blobs.
safety_notes: Playbooks are operational guidance, not promotion authority.
Frontier findings remain pointer-only until screened and validated.
Repos keep local authority and decide whether to adopt suggestions.

assets.name: Language Frontier Research Harness
use_when: A repo finds a Python, Rust, mixed-language, or future-language source that may improve AI coding.
DAD needs to decide whether a frontier coding idea belongs in an idiom card, buildout guide, tactic, or harness eval.
A coding agent wants to report an underused feature, tool, crate, package, or proof surface back to DAD.
does_not_apply_when: The idea lacks a source pointer, safe summary, applicability limit, and validation idea.
The evidence is copied third-party docs, copied source, private rows, raw logs, credentials, or benchmark-only claims.
The target repo has not approved DAD pointers or local validation for the language/tool.
safety_notes: This harness is a first-pass gate, not promotion authority.
repo-local source_package means this asset was created in DAD, not imported from a zip or external source.
Source pointers and trust tiers never authorize copying external content.
Language-frontier guidance requires local validation and repo authority before adoption.

assets.name: DAD Local Read-Only MCP Host Adapters
use_when: A supported AI host needs the existing local read-only DAD graph MCP server.
Another repository needs a reviewed pointer to the canonical DAD MCP invocation without a vendor-specific fork.
An operator needs to verify cross-host command, tool, transport, and authority parity before installation.
does_not_apply_when: The requested integration needs remote transport, source mutation, Git execution, or vendor API credentials.
The host or target repository has not approved MCP installation and trust.
The configured Python executable or DAD hub has not passed an initialize handshake.
safety_notes: All templates resolve to one local stdio server and deny remote and execution authority.
Machine-specific paths are rendered only at installation time and are absent from the reusable asset.
Host installation, trust, restart, and downstream adoption remain separate human gates.
The asset was authored locally from first-party host configuration contracts and contains no third-party implementation code or credentials.

assets.name: DAD 9-Layer Learning Address Model
use_when: A repo needs a compact way to record digital asset identity, claims, validation, provenance, retrieval tags, and learning outcomes.
DAD needs to connect original fixes, derivative fixes, context deltas, and future lookup triggers.
A workflow or orchestration asset needs to be represented by a small card and refs instead of pasted long-form instructions.
An agent needs to understand why addresses complement graph edges.
does_not_apply_when: The record is one-off and does not need future-agent retrieval.
The address model would add ceremony without improving routing, evidence, provenance, validation, or learning.
A source repo has its own address canon and DAD should only store pointer metadata.
safety_notes: Use compact refs and IDs; do not inline raw logs, private rows, or long workflow text.
Layer 9 is DAD's learning/adaptation layer and remains subject to versioned evolution.
The model is a coordinate system for graph nodes and records, not proof of graph truth or source authority.
Frontier AI recommendations are candidate-only until migration tests and review pass.
